answer: Slashable stake bonding mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital into escrow before transacting. An attacker attempting to cultivate an orchard of fake identities faces a basalt barrier of locked collateral incurred per registration. A cryptographic beacon periodically audits agent activity to trigger slashing for verifiable faults. A major limitation is that capital lockup favors wealthy incumbents and imposes prohibitive onboarding costs on legitimate low-budget agents.
